title: Cellular Network Performance Analyst
description:
About the job

Delart is home to a team of world-class engineers and project leaders dedicated to developing the next generation of advanced networking technologies, consumer devices, and innovative technology solutions. Trusted by some of the world’s leading technology companies, we deliver highly scalable, mission-critical solutions that power both consumer and business applications globally. Since our founding in 2017, we have been at the forefront of designing cutting-edge networking, telecommunications, and consumer products, while driving end-to-end project execution and creating transformative technology applications.

Overview
Join our team as a network analytics specialist focused on enhancing end-to-end cellular network performance and improving application-layer Quality of Experience (QoE). You will design and implement advanced analytics solutions to extract actionable insights from massive volumes of network data, driving the evolution of mobile network services.
Responsibilities

• Analyze end-to-end cellular network performance to identify bottlenecks and areas for enhancement.

• Collaborate with network engineers and operators to optimize application-layer QoE based on analytical findings.

• Design and implement scalable data processing pipelines for processing large-scale network datasets.

• Develop analytics code using Python, R, and SQL to extract and interpret insights on application-layer performance.

• Conduct comprehensive data collection campaigns in partnership with network operators to gather, validate, and analyze real-world network data.

Minimum Qualifications

• Deep understanding of cellular network protocols and systems (e.g., LTE, 5G NR).

• Advanced proficiency in Python, R, and SQL for data analytics and solution development.

• Demonstrated experience analyzing end-to-end cellular network data to generate actionable insights.

• Proven track record collaborating with network operators for data collection and analysis.

• Ability to architect and implement large-scale analytics solutions for network data processing.

• 4+ years of hands-on experience in the network domain of mobile systems (e.g., 5G, LTE).

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct experience partnering with cellular network operators on data gathering and collaborative analysis.

• Familiarity with application-layer QoE optimization techniques and advanced performance analysis.

• Expertise with modern data processing frameworks (e.g., Spark, Hadoop) and cloud-based analytics solutions (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).

• Background working with diverse and high-volume network datasets in complex network environments.

Benefits

Delart provides competitive benefits and compensation across all regions where we operate. In the United States , our benefits package includes premium PPO and HMO medical insurance, dental and vision coverage, flexible spending accounts (FSA), life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, a company-matched 401(k) plan, and a generous paid time off policy.

Join us in shaping the future of technology. Apply today!

Delart is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace for all employees. We strictly prohibit discrimination or harassment of any kind based on race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability, genetics, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Research Intern, Frontier Agents (Winter 2027)
description:
About the Role

The Agents team investigates how to build, align, and scale frontier AI systems that can tackle complex, multi-step tasks and workflows across text and speech, with a particular focus on agentic and scientific domains. Our work sits at the intersection of agent capabilities, human-computer interaction, and infrastructure-from designing post-training methods for agentic behavior to developing evaluation frameworks for open-ended tasks where traditional metrics fall short. 

As a research intern, you will work on problems at the frontier of agentic AI, where challenges in alignment, reliability, and scalability are deeply intertwined. Projects may involve developing new training recipes for self-learning and long-horizon reasoning, curating datasets for non-deterministic scientific and agentic tasks, studying failure modes in agentic behavior, or building infrastructure that enables agent operations at scale. You'll operate in a space where algorithmic innovation, dataset and interaction design, and systems work come together to push the boundaries of what AI agents can reliably accomplish.

Responsibilities

• Research and implement novel techniques in one or more of our focus areas

• Design and conduct rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses

• Document findings in scientific publications and blog posts

• Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team

Requirements

• Currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Information Science, or a related field

• Publications at leading ML, NLP, or speech conferences or journals (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, *ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech)

• Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals

• Experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, etc.)

• Understanding of how LLMs work

• Strong programming skills in Python

• Familiarity with Transformer architectures and recent developments in foundation models

Example Research Directions

• Training, developing, and evaluating frontier models, especially in the domain of agentic tasks and workflows

• Designing and curating datasets for frontier agents alignment and post-training

• Studying failure modes and developing safety paradigms for agentic behavior

• Research new recipes (for RL or test time scaling) for self-learning and long-context tasks completion

• Building agents that act on spoken input to carry out complex, multi-step tasks

• Developing ML infrastructure that can power agent operations at scale

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

Internship Program Details

Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span January 4th to April 9th.

Compensation

We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. Our hourly rates are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.

title: Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence. Through data and advocacy, TfG drives action to break cycles of violence and ensure prevention, healing, and justice. By connecting the dots between understanding the problem, identifying effective solutions, tracking progress, and mobilizing for action, TfG creates a synergistic effect that amplifies its impact and drives toward its ultimate goal of creating a safer world for children and adolescents.
Grounded in 19 years of data from the Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS), which provide a clear picture of the problem, we drive coordinated action through three initiatives that collectively contribute to ending violence against children. The Safe Futures Solutions Hub shares evidence and practice-based knowledge to inform effective prevention and response efforts, ensuring access to proven solutions across sectors. The Brave Movement mobilizes survivors and allies worldwide to drive political will, influence policy, and ensure that inaction is not an option. Finally, the Out of the Shadows Index tracks countries’ progress in addressing violence, providing an accountability framework and benchmark for advocacy. Together, these initiatives form a powerful model that transforms evidence into collective action for prevention, healing, and justice.
We are a nimble and highly impactful team that continues to grow and evolve. We work with a broad range of organizations, researchers, and advocates to drive change.
Position Overview
The Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis plays a key role in strengthening Together for Girls ’ financial planning, analysis, and grant financial management across its US and European entities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance, this role leads and supports budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis, grant financial management, and proposal costing, translating complex financial information into clear insights that support organizational decision-making.
Working closely with Finance, Development, Grants Management, and Program teams, the Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis will help ensure TfG effectively plans and manages resources across a diverse portfolio of donor-funded programs. The role requires both strong technical financial skills and the ability to partner with non-finance colleagues, identify emerging financial risks and opportunities, and develop practical tools and analysis that strengthen financial management across the organization.

title: Senior Asset Pipeline Engineer, Sim-Ready Content
description: About Genesis AI Genesis AI builds the simulation platform powering the next generation of robotics and embodied AI. Our flagship product, Genesis World, is a unified multi-physics simulation engine paired with Nyx, our in-house GPU-accelerated, path-traced photorealistic renderer. Together they provide a platform for training robotics and embodied AI at scale; letting teams simulate complex physical worlds with high fidelity and speed, from a laptop to datacenter-grade GPUs, and close the gap between simulation and the real world. About the Role A simulator is only as useful as the content that runs inside it. Training embodied agents at scale means large volumes of assets that are simultaneously physically valid and visually convincing and that is a pipeline problem before it is an art problem. We're hiring a Senior Engineer to build the path from raw input to sim-ready asset: geometry from a range of sources going in; clean meshes, correct collision proxies, plausible physical properties, materials that hold up under a path tracer, and reliable metadata coming out. The bar is throughput and repeatability. An asset that needs a human pass to be usable doesn't scale, so the pipeline has to make good decisions on its own and flag the cases where it can't. Part of that autonomy comes from agents embedded in the graph itself. Nodes can call models to produce input content, drive generation, pick parameters, interpret a mesh before deciding how to treat it, or judge whether a result is acceptable. Making that reliable is its own engineering problem: agents are non-deterministic, they fail in ways a mesh operator doesn't, and they need guardrails, structured outputs, retries and verification around them. title: Senior Staff Quantum Scientist

description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Role Overview

Role:

We are looking for a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist to join our Science team at IonQ. In this role, you will take a leading role in our research efforts, driving experimental efforts and the architecture of our future generation quantum systems.

We are pioneering advancements in quantum computing by utilising trapped ion technology and our proprietary laser-free quantum control methods. Our research and development efforts build on our fully integrated quantum processors that can be fabricated within standard silicon foundries. This unique approach allows us to leverage the highest-performing qubit technology while ensuring scalability and manufacturability using existing semiconductor fabrication technology.

We approach quantum computing with a focus on minimising errors, striving to achieve ultra-low gate errors at scale. Our immediate objective is to develop functional quantum computers within the NISQ regime, aiming to construct fault-tolerant machines that require minimal QEC overhead. Our recent breakthroughs include achieving 99.97% fidelity in two-qubit gates and 99.9992% fidelity in single-qubit operations without error correction, setting new industry standards for performance.

Responsibilities:

As a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist you will be at the forefront of our research and development, taking a leading role within our experimental science team. You will be responsible for driving innovation in coherent control, calibration, and benchmarking at scale, with a particular focus on enabling ultra-low error rates and system reliability across larger trapped-ion devices.

You will work hands-on with our current hardware, with work spanning design, debugging, and executing experiments, developing novel control schemes, and pushing the boundaries of system performance.

Beyond hands-on experiments, you will help shape technical direction, mentor junior scientists, and ensure our work translates into scalable, fault-tolerant systems.

Key responsibilities include:

• Lead the prototyping and characterisation of advanced coherent control schemes for trapped-ion qubits using laser and microwave fields.

• Drive system-level benchmarking and optimisation, ensuring near-term devices achieve world-leading performance and stability.

• Validate and integrate new trap technologies (e.g. on-chip electronics or photonics) to support scaling towards error-corrected architectures.

• Guide junior scientists in experimental design, analysis, and presentation of results.

• Represent IonQ at conferences and external collaborations.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Space Imaging team is seeking a Systems Engineer to join our team. The Imaging Space team is responsible for system architecture definition, trade analyses, and modeling/validating system performance for spaceborne EO/IR systems.

In this role, you will be responsible for defining active EO/IR system architectures. You will perform radiometric performance modeling as well as laboratory, ground, and flight testing. To predict real-world performance, you will also model atmospheric and environmental effects for land, sea, and air targets. You will leverage your analyses to inform system-level architectural trades. As needed, you will also lead small teams of engineers from concept ideation through system definition and development.

You should have a track record of successfully working on fast-paced, highly technical, interdisciplinary teams. Proficiency in analytical toolchains or languages (e.g., MATLAB, Python) is required. Experience with industry standard EO/IR modeling software packages (e.g. MODTRAN, SPIRITS, AFSIM) is a plus. Prior experience working with space sensors and systems is highly desirable.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Define system architectures via detailed trade studies and analyses.

• Adapt or derive physics-based models of sensor system performance and derive requirements based on those models.

• Take ownership over the development of prototype sensor systems in a lab environment.

• Support both laboratory-based and field-based experiments and demonstrations.

• Engage technically with the hardware, software, and mission teams to define, integrate, and deliver high performance systems to our customers.

• Validate models against laboratory and real-world data.

• Coordinate and communicate with both external & internal stakeholders with varying degrees of technical background.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Model development and validation in one or more domains relevant to remote sensing

• Ability to decompose complex systems into functional parts, with clearly defined interfaces and requirements for each.

• Experience in system design and development from initial concept through test and delivery to customer.

• Strong laboratory skills (rapid prototyping, design of experiments) and familiarity with opto-electrical test and measurement equipment.

• Willingness to travel to test sites, as needed.

• Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Knowledge of current and next-generation advanced sensing systems and platforms

• Active and passive sensing domain experience (e.g., LiDAR, EO/IR, Radar)

• Experience with laser systems, including opto-mechanical scanning and beam steering techniques.

• Knowledge of electro-mechanical control systems, including their performance requirements and verification methodologies.

• Experience with LiDAR/Radar signal processing techniques, and knowledge of their implementation on real-time embedded platforms (FPGA, MCU, etc.).

• Experience with signature and/or scenario modeling/software packages (MODTRAN, SPIRITS, AFSIM).

• Space domain experience (architecting sensors for operation in space environments)

title: Speech Therapist
description:
Join Hire Hangar and work with fast-growing global companies while building a long-term career.

Location: Lawrenceville/Loganville/Hoschton/Peachtree Corners, GA

Employment Type: Full-Time

Compensation: $90,000-$120,000/year

ROLE OVERVIEW

We are seeking a compassionate and skilled Pediatric Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team. In this role, you will evaluate and treat children with a wide range of speech, language, and feeding/swallowing needs, working closely with families to guide them in understanding their child's areas of need and strengths. A central part of this position is helping families support their child's intervention and carryover of skills at home, at school, and in the community, ensuring progress made in session translates into everyday life.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Conduct comprehensive speech, language, articulation, fluency, voice, and feeding/swallowing evaluations for pediatric clients

• Develop individualized treatment plans with measurable goals based on assessment findings and each child's developmental level

• Provide direct, evidence-based therapy for a caseload of pediatric clients with diverse communication and feeding disorders

• Guide families in understanding their child's areas of need and strengths, translating clinical findings into clear, actionable information

• Partner with parents and caregivers to support carryover of skills and strategies at home, at school, and in the community

• Coordinate and communicate with teachers, pediatricians, occupational and physical therapists, and other providers involved in the child's care

• Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation, including evaluation reports, SOAP notes, progress notes, and insurance-required paperwork

• Track client progress toward goals on an ongoing basis and adjust treatment plans as needed

• Participate in team meetings, case conferences, and school-based meetings (e.g., IEP/IFSP) as needed

• Educate parents and caregivers on home exercise programs, strategies, and tools to reinforce therapy outside of sessions

• Stay current with best practices, research, and continuing education in pediatric speech-language pathology

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Master's degree in Speech-Language Pathology from a program accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation (CAA)

• Active Georgia state license in Speech-Language Pathology (or eligibility to obtain), and ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP)

• Minimum of 2 years of clinical experience working with pediatric clients across a range of speech, language, and feeding/swallowing disorders

• Strong understanding of child development and evidence-based assessment and treatment approaches for pediatric communication and feeding disorders

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to build rapport with children and explain clinical concepts clearly and empathetically to parents and caregivers

• Proven ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and to coordinate treatment carryover across home, school, and community settings

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience supervising Clinical Fellows (CFs) or graduate student clinicians

• Specialized training or certification (e.g., PROMPT, feeding and swallowing certifications, AAC)

• Bilingual or multilingual skills

• Prior experience in a private practice or pediatric outpatient setting

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGY

• Electronic health record / practice management systems (e.g., SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, WebPT, or similar)

• Standardized assessment tools (e.g., CELF, PLS-5, GFTA, or comparable pediatric speech/language batteries)

• Teletherapy platforms for virtual sessions, where applicable

• Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) devices and apps

• Microsoft Office / Google Workspace for documentation, scheduling, and reporting

title: Manager, Talent Account Management
description:
Overview
Together, We Enhance Innovation and Growth
The Manager, Talent Account Management leads the team of Talent Account Managers (TAMs) who run i2G's hiring process from intake to close. The TAMs own the hiring manager relationship and the candidate experience once a candidate enters an active process. This Manager makes sure that work is focused on the right roles, delivered to a consistent standard, and measured in a way the business can trust.
The role is accountable for delivery outcomes, reporting, customer satisfaction and escalations. It works from the priority order set jointly with the Capacity Planning Manager, so that TAM time goes to the roles that matter most to i2G's contracts and markets. It operates on Kastle Systems' talent platforms (iCIMS, LinkedIn and Indeed) and draws its candidate supply from Kastle's Sourcing team.
This is a leadership and delivery role, not a sourcing role and not a demand-planning role. It does not own the demand forecast, which sits with the Capacity Planning Manager. It does not own top-of-funnel sourcing, which sits with Kastle's Sourcing team. It owns what happens between those two: turning qualified leads into hires, and doing it well.
Reporting and working relationships

•
Chief Operating Officer, i2G (direct). Sets business priorities for the team, evaluates performance and is the escalation point for delivery and resourcing issues.

•
Senior Director, Talent Acquisition, Kastle Systems (indirect). Sets recruiting process standards, platform usage and compliance expectations, and partners on team practices and reporting.

•
Capacity Planning Manager, i2G (peer). Owns the labor demand forecast and the rolling requisition priority order. The two roles agree together where TAM effort goes each month.

•
Kastle Sourcing team (upstream partner). Supplies sourced and inbound candidates to the TAMs. This Manager owns the quality feedback loop back to Sourcing.

•
i2G hiring managers and branch leadership (customers). The people the TAMs serve. This Manager is the senior point of contact for their satisfaction and their escalations.

Responsibilities
Key responsibilities
1. Team leadership and coaching

• Lead, coach and develop three Talent Account Managers. Set clear expectations, run regular one-to-ones and case reviews, and give direct performance feedback.

• Assign requisition portfolios to TAMs based on priority, complexity, market and workload, and rebalance as demand shifts.

• Set and audit the standard for the TAM role: intake quality, screening rigor, submittal quality, interview coordination, feedback turnaround, offer preparation and close.

• Coach TAMs on running difficult conversations with hiring managers, including pushing back on unrealistic requirements or slow decisions.

• Hire, onboard and backfill TAMs as needed, and maintain a development path for the team.

2. Prioritization and alignment with capacity planning

• Work with the Capacity Planning Manager as the single point of alignment between operations demand and TAM delivery.

• Run the team from the rolling 90-day requisition forecast and its agreed priority order. Confirm each month which roles get TAM focus first.

• Make sure TAM effort follows priority, not volume of requests or the loudest hiring manager. Flag when priorities conflict or when demand exceeds what the team can deliver.

• Take part in the monthly talent acquisition and operations review with data, recommendations and follow-through on decisions.

• Raise early warning when a priority role is at risk, including the revenue or delivery consequence, so trade-offs are made with full information.

3. Hiring manager partnership and customer satisfaction

• Own the operating relationship with i2G hiring managers and branch leadership at the leadership level, and hold the TAMs to a consistent service standard.

• Set and enforce an intake standard so every requisition has a clear profile, priority, compensation range and interview plan befo

title: Refrigeration Technician
description:
Job Description:  As a Refrigeration Technician, you will work with the maintenance team to maintain, troubleshoot, and repair HVAC, refrigeration and facilities equipment to maintain critical temperatures and improve reliability of our systems. This role is the resident expert in refrigeration systems. 

Shift: Monday to Friday - 3:00pm to 11:30pm or 4:00pm to 12:30am

You will...

• Maintain and operate industrial refrigeration systems including large rack systems, split systems, blast chillers, cooling towers and ancillary equipment.

• Lead and educate compliance with all safety, food safety, and security standards. 

• Perform preventive maintenance and routine inspections on assigned refrigeration and HVAC systems and ancillary equipment as needed. 

• Perform troubleshooting of assigned out of service equipment and correct issues, act as an escalation point for lower-level technicians, and escalate to leadership and/or vendors as needed for additional troubleshooting.

• Document all work in the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) and ticketing systems as appropriate.

• Mentor all maintenance personnel in developing appropriate skill sets and knowledge of equipment specializing in refrigeration.

• Lead root cause analysis of major downtime events.

• Act as a network resource for technical issues and lead network-wide root cause analysis.

• Develop maintenance personnel knowledge on intermediate to advanced refrigeration processes, tools and techniques.

• Audit maintenance personnel work and provide feedback to improve performance and quality.

• Audit vendor work to provide feedback to leadership on quality of work and SLA performance.

• Write and/or modify PMs to standardize across the network and increase effectiveness.

• Repair and perform predictive and preventative maintenance procedures on CO2 and Freon refrigeration systems including, but not limited to compressors, pumps, fans, heat exchangers, glycol systems, various industrial utility systems, motors, and power distribution systems.

• Give direction and/or training to entry level refrigeration technicians including, but not limited to day-to-day operations, inspections and inspection techniques, basic repairs and repair techniques, and conformance to all state, local, and HelloFresh regulations and policies.

• Perform building project work as assigned.

You have...

• 4-6 years of experience with refrigeration repair and maintenance in an industrial setting, 

• Advanced understanding of rack system refrigeration and associated equipment.

• Experience with repair and maintenance of glycol systems, heat exchangers, HVAC, and water chiller systems.

• Experience with electrical systems including single and three phase motor systems, power distribution, and low voltage controls with the ability to troubleshoot to the component level.

• Current Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Section 608 certification.

• All necessary regulatory licenses required by local municipalities to work in the field of industrial refrigeration.

• Ability to demonstrate excellent work habits in line with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP’s).

• Ability to conform to all OSHA, PSM, HAZMAT, and HelloFresh safety programs and regulations.

• Ability to demonstrate understanding of proper handling and recycling procedures for chlorofluorocarbon (CFC), hydrochlorofluorocarbon (HCFC), Hydrofluro-Olefins (HFO), CO2, and other industry standard refrigerant types.

• Ability to safely replace mechanical and electrical components including motors, motor starters, switches, solenoids, pumps, refrigeration valves, compressors, and auxiliary refrigeration equipment.

• Experience working with a wide range of networked refrigeration controls platforms.

• Ability to withstand walking, lifting, bending, stooping, climbing ladders, walking on roofs, and working in confined spaces.

• Basic computer skills.

• Ability to read and understand drawings,

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Implicit Signals
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our team builds classification and evaluation systems that give post-training and research teams fast, reliable feedback on model behavior. We combine machine learning and production engineering to make these capabilities accurate, efficient, and useful at scale, helping researchers assess changes and improve models and products.

We work closely with research teams to develop useful measurements and make them practical to run. Our work spans classifier development, rigorous evaluation, and efficient production inference, with ownership from initial experimentation through deployment and continued improvement.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to develop new classification and evaluation capabilities and bring them into production. You’ll help turn open-ended questions about model behavior into well-defined ML problems, build methods that address them, and establish how reliably those methods work.

This role combines traditional machine learning, model evaluation, and real-time engineering. You’ll own classifiers throughout their lifecycle, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation, deployment, and production inference. You’ll work closely with researchers to identify valuable problems and with software engineers to make promising approaches useful at scale.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Build, deploy, and operate production classification and evaluation systems that provide useful feedback to post-training and research teams.

- Optimize production inference, including model serving, batching, caching, throughput, latency, compute utilization, and cost.

- Train and optimize classifiers using supervised fine-tuning and distillation, validating quality and efficiency before deployment.

- Own the reliability and observability of deployed classifiers, diagnose production issues, and improve their performance over time.

- Design rigorous evaluations that assess accuracy, calibration, generalization, and potential measurement bias while guiding production tradeoffs.

- Partner with software engineers to integrate models into reliable execution systems and support safe rollouts.

- Build reusable engineering tools that make classifier training, evaluation, deployment, and iteration faster and more repeatable.

- Work with post-training researchers and data scientists to translate their needs into modeling objectives, evaluation criteria, and production requirements.

YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE

- Experience taking ML projects from problem formulation and experimentation through production deployment.

- Strong foundations in supervised learning, statistics, and experimental design.

- Practical experience evaluating models, investigating systematic errors, and working with imperfect labels.

- Strong software engineering skills and the ability to build maintainable production ML systems.

- Experience reasoning about inference performance and the tradeoffs between quality, latency, and compute cost.

- The ability to combine careful scientific judgment with a practical approach to shipping and operating software.

- Comfort working closely with researchers and engineers on open-ended problems.

- Fluency in using AI agents to move quickly across multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

- Experience with model distillation, representation learning, calibration, or efficient inference is a plus.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Junior Payroll Specialist
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company - we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.
The Role
The Veeva Systems EMEA Payroll team is hiring for an ambitious, detail-oriented Junior Payroll Specialist with 1-2 years of Hungarian payroll experience who is ready to accelerate their career in a dynamic, high-performance culture. In this role, you will take true E2E ownership of Hungarian payroll calculations while collaborating closely with supportive senior team members to develop your skills in multi-country European (EMEA) operations.

You will step beyond local statutory processing to tackle new intellectual challenges, building deep expertise in international compliance, vendor management, and complex cross-border payroll.
What You'll Do

• End-to-End Processing: Execute the full payroll cycle for a designated portfolio of several EU countries, including data input, validation, calculation, and final transmission to external payroll providers

• Data Integrity & Reconciliation: Perform reconciliations of payroll data against source systems. Investigate and resolve all discrepancies quickly and accurately

• Tax & Statutory Compliance: Ensure strict adherence to all local tax, social security, and statutory requirements

• Variable Compensation: Accurately process complex payroll inputs, including bonuses, commissions, equity transactions (RSUs/Stock Options), expatriate allowances, and complex termination payments

• Analytical Support: Utilize strong analytical skills and proficiency in advanced Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, complex formulas)

• Customer Service: Provide prompt, professional, and confidential support to employees regarding complex payroll calculations, deductions, and tax inquiries, ensuring a high level of employee satisfaction

• Internal Partnership: Collaborate seamlessly with internal teams (HR, Finance) to ensure accurate employee classifications, benefits administration, and payroll transactions

• Audit Support: Assist with internal and external payroll audits by preparing necessary documentation, ensuring compliance with internal controls (e.g., SOX compliance)

• Ad hoc - perform ad hoc tasks as and when assigned by the payroll manager

Requirements

• 1+ years of professional experience managing end-to-end payroll processing, preferably in a multinational environment

• Proven proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including advanced data analysis and reconciliation techniques

• Experience working with a major HRIS system (Workday) would be an advantage

• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced environment

• Fluency in verbal and written English is required

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.

• Follow the application process and submit your resume.

• Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.

• Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email
